reason: The cited evidence E2 directly supports all key premises by describing the exact alloy, coating thickness, formation of a dense HfO₂ layer, reduced weight gain, and prevention of surface degradation under high-temperature oxidation, with no misrepresentation. E1 provides only general background and is not needed for the specific claims.
premises: A thin Hf coating on VZrHfNbTa HEA forms a dense HfO₂ protective layer during high-temperature oxidation.
The HfO₂ layer reduces oxygen ingress and improves oxidation resistance.
The coated alloy shows much lower weight gain than the uncoated alloy.
The coating prevents surface degradation like dents and pulverization.
The effect is demonstrated at ~1000°C in air.
